passages.title: Daily routine
sentences: I usually wake up at seven o'clock and start my day with a cup of tea.
After breakfast, I spend about an hour checking my emails and planning my work.
In the evening, I prefer to go for a short walk instead of watching television.
Getting enough sleep is really important to me, so I try to go to bed before eleven.

passages.title: My hometown
sentences: I was born and raised in a medium-sized city in the north of China.
My hometown is famous for its old town, which attracts a lot of tourists every summer.
Compared with big cities, the pace of life there is much slower and more relaxed.
The one thing I don't like about it is that the public transport is not very convenient.

passages.title: A hobby I enjoy
sentences: In my free time, I enjoy taking photos of street scenes and ordinary people.
I started this hobby about three years ago, when my friend gave me a second-hand camera.
Photography teaches me to notice small details that I used to ignore.
I don't plan to become a professional, but it gives me a lot of pleasure.

passages.title: My favourite season
sentences: My favourite season is autumn because the weather is cool and comfortable.
In autumn, the leaves turn red and gold, and the whole city looks different.
Autumn is also the season when I feel most energetic and focused on my goals.

passages.title: Using technology
sentences: Technology has changed the way I work, study and even relax.
My smartphone helps me keep in touch with friends who live far away.
However, I try to limit my screen time in the evening so that I can sleep better.
I think the key is to use technology as a tool, not to let it control my life.

passages.title: Healthy eating
sentences: Eating well does not have to be complicated or expensive.
I try to cook at home most days and avoid ordering too much fast food.
A simple meal with vegetables, rice and some fish is both cheap and healthy.
Drinking enough water is just as important as choosing the right food.

passages.title: Learning English
sentences: I have been learning English for many years, but my speaking is still my weakest point.
The best way to improve is to practise a little every day instead of studying for hours once a week.
I find that reading aloud helps me remember new words and sentence patterns.
Making mistakes is a normal part of learning, so I try not to be afraid of them.

passages.title: A memorable trip
sentences: Last summer, I took a trip to a small island with two of my closest friends.
We spent most of our days swimming in the sea and walking along the coast.
One evening, we got lost on our way back to the hotel and had to ask a local for help.
Although the trip was not perfect, it taught me that travelling together can make friendships stronger.
I still look at the photos from that trip whenever I feel stressed.

passages.title: My best friend
sentences: My best friend and I have known each other since we were in primary school.
We share a similar sense of humour, so we can laugh about almost anything.
What I admire most about her is that she always keeps her promises.
Even though we now live in different cities, we still talk on the phone every week.

passages.title: Working from home
sentences: Working from home has both advantages and disadvantages.
On the positive side, I save a lot of time because I do not have to commute every day.
On the other hand, it is easy to feel lonely and to work longer than I should.
To stay productive, I keep a clear schedule and take short breaks between tasks.

passages.title: Protecting the environment
sentences: Protecting the environment is everyone's responsibility, not just the government's job.
Small actions, such as saving water and using public transport, can make a real difference.
I try to carry a reusable bag and avoid buying products with too much plastic packaging.
If everyone changes just one habit, the total effect will be enormous.

passages.title: My plans for the future
sentences: In the future, I would like to study or work abroad for a couple of years.
My main goal is to improve my English so that I can communicate with confidence.
I also hope to find a job that lets me keep learning new skills.
Of course, plans can change, so I try to stay open to new opportunities.

passages.title: Morning Routines
sentences: I usually wake up around six thirty, even on weekends.
The first thing I do is drink a large glass of warm water.
Then I spend twenty minutes jogging around my neighborhood before breakfast.
A steady morning routine keeps my energy stable for the whole day.
If I skip it, I feel sluggish and easily distracted at work.

passages.title: Public Libraries
sentences: The library near my home was rebuilt last year, and it is now a quiet, bright space.
You can borrow up to ten books at a time and keep them for a month.
Many students go there to study because the reading rooms stay open until nine.
I like the atmosphere: everyone is focused, and nobody talks on the phone.
Libraries are no longer just about books; ours also offers free lectures and coding classes.

passages.title: Online Shopping
sentences: These days I buy almost everything online, from shoes to fresh fruit.
Delivery is remarkably fast; most orders arrive within twenty-four hours.
The main risk is that pictures sometimes look better than the real product.
So I always read the reviews carefully before placing an order.
Overall, online shopping has saved me a huge amount of time.

passages.title: Keeping Pets
sentences: My family has kept a golden retriever for five years, and he is part of the family now.
Walking him every evening has genuinely improved my fitness.
Pets also teach children responsibility and patience.
Of course, they are a long-term commitment: food, vaccines and vet visits all cost money.
I would only recommend a pet to people who can stay at home regularly.

passages.title: Weekend Activities
sentences: On Saturdays I usually meet friends for badminton in the morning.
Sundays are quieter: I cook a proper meal and catch up on reading.
I try to keep at least one afternoon completely free of screens.
It sounds simple, but it really helps me recharge for the week ahead.
When the weather is good, we take a short trip to the countryside instead.

passages.title: Social Media
sentences: I spend about an hour a day on social media, mostly watching short videos.
It keeps me connected with old classmates, which I genuinely value.
However, the endless recommendations can easily eat up your whole evening.
So I set a daily limit and turn my phone off after ten o'clock.
Used carefully, social media is a tool; used carelessly, it becomes a habit.

passages.title: Learning Languages
sentences: I have been learning English for several years, mostly on my commute.
Listening to podcasts works better for me than memorizing word lists.
The hardest part is speaking, because I rarely meet native speakers.
So I record myself answering questions and compare it with the original audio.
Small daily practice matters far more than one long session on the weekend.

passages.title: City Parks
sentences: Our city has built several small parks in the past few years.
Research suggests that small, nearby parks matter more than one large one far away.
Every evening these parks fill with children, dancers and dog walkers.
They also cool the streets down noticeably in summer.
To me, a city without parks is like a house without windows.

passages.title: Home Cooking
sentences: I started cooking during a busy work period, purely to save money.
Surprisingly, it became my favorite way to relax after a long day.
Home cooking is healthier too, because you control the oil and salt.
My signature dish is a simple tomato and egg stir-fry.
Nothing beats the smell of fresh food in your own kitchen.

passages.title: Public Transport
sentences: I take the subway to work every day, and it takes about forty minutes.
I use that time to listen to English podcasts or read a few pages.
Public transport is far cheaper than driving once you count parking and fuel.
The rush hour can be crowded, but the trains run every three minutes.
For me, it is the most predictable way to cross the city.

passages.title: Mobile Phones
sentences: My phone is basically an office, a library and a cinema in my pocket.
I pay bills, book tickets and even attend meetings on it.
The downside is that it is hard to put down, especially before bed.
Recently I started charging it outside the bedroom, and my sleep improved.
A phone should serve you, not the other way round.

passages.title: Seasons and Weather
sentences: I love autumn best, because the air is cool and the sky stays clear.
Summer in my city is hot and humid, and everyone hides indoors at noon.
Winter is short but the heating makes my room extremely dry.
Spring is beautiful, though the wind can be strong and dusty.
People in my hometown always say there are only two seasons: summer and winter.

passages.title: Museums
sentences: Our city museum reopened last month after two years of renovation.
Admission is free now, and there is a new gallery for local history.
Guided tours run every hour and are well worth joining.
I once found an exhibition about my own neighborhood's past.
Museums remind people that a city is not just buildings and traffic.

passages.title: Photography
sentences: I got into photography when I bought my first smartphone with a good camera.
At first I photographed everything; later I learned to wait for the right light.
Early morning and sunset give the best colors by far.
Photography has taught me to notice small details in ordinary streets.
The best camera is simply the one you carry every day.

passages.title: Neighborhood Life
sentences: I live in an old neighborhood where everyone knows each other.
The vegetable seller saves the freshest stock for regular customers.
When my family moved in, our neighbors brought us dinner for a week.
Such close ties are rare in new high-rise communities.
A friendly neighborhood makes a city feel like home.

passages.title: Local Markets
sentences: The morning market near my home opens at six and is busiest by seven.
Vendors shout their prices, and bargaining is part of the experience.
Everything is fresher and cheaper than in the supermarket.
You also run into neighbors, so shopping doubles as social time.
I honestly enjoy the noise and energy of a busy market.

passages.title: Rainy Days
sentences: Rainy days completely change the rhythm of my city.
The streets quiet down, and the air smells fresh and clean.
I used to find rain depressing, but now I enjoy it with a cup of tea.
The only trouble is traffic: every taxi seems to be taken.
Still, a slow rainy afternoon is perfect for reading.

passages.title: Cycling in the City
sentences: More people in my city are commuting by bicycle than ever before.
The city has added protected bike lanes along the main roads.
Cycling beats the bus for trips under five kilometers.
It is cheaper, faster at rush hour, and good exercise at the same time.
The main risk remains reckless car drivers near intersections.

passages.title: Street Food
sentences: My city is famous for its street food, especially after sunset.
My personal favorite is grilled tofu with chili sauce.
Good street stalls rely on regular customers, so quality stays high.
Hygiene has improved a lot since the city introduced food ratings.
For many locals, street food is a weekend tradition, not just a meal.

passages.title: Quiet Places
sentences: Every city needs quiet places where people can slow down.
My refuge is a small teahouse hidden behind an old temple.
The owner keeps two cats and never plays any music.
I go there to read, think, or simply watch the rain.
In a noisy world, silence has become something you have to look for.
